You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Diagonal pattern: 9s at (0,0),(0,2),(1,1),(1,3),(2,1),(2,3),(3,?)... Row 8: 1 9 1 9 1 9 1 → all gaps between 9s filled. Row 11 all ones, no change. Row 3 all ones no change. So rule: fill each 1 that has a 9 on both left and right in same row? Check row 0 col 4,5,6: to right of (0,2)9, no 9 to right, not filled. Col 1: 9 left at (0,0), 9 right at (0,2) → filled 2. Yes!

Check vertical? Only rows changed. Row 5: 9 1 9 → 9 2 9. Row 1: 1 9 1 9 → 1 9 2 9. Row 2 same. Row 6 same. Row 9: 1 9 1 9 → 1 9 2 9. Row 10: 1 9 1 9 1 9 1 → 1 9 2 9 2 9 1? Output row 10: 1 9 2 9 2 9 1 ✓.

Column 1: (1,1)9,(2,1)9 adjacent. Check column with vertical gap: output didn't add vertical-only fills... e.g. col 5 row... Actually check whether any fill cell has 9 above and below but not left/right. Row 8 col 5: filled 2, has 9 at (8,4) and (8,6) left/right. Seems horizontal only. But maybe the rule is fill gaps along the diagonal lines? Diagonal lines: (0,0),(1,1),(2,1)... hmm (1,1) and (2,1) are vertical. Actually shape is like a zigzag. Simpler: horizontal between-rule works for all demo rows. Check demo col-by-col to confirm no vertical fills needed: output row3 all 1s, input row3 all 1s fine. Row 11 all 1s unchanged.

Hmm, but wait — could also be "fill gap between 9s along anti-diagonal rays"? Horizontal rule suffices; verify no counterexample: any output 2 whose row doesn't have 9 on both sides? Check each 2 in output: row0c1: 9s at c0,c2 ✓. row1c2: 9 at c1,c3 ✓. row2c2 ✓. row4c3 ✓. row5c1 ✓. row6c2 ✓. row7c1,c3 ✓. row8c2,c4 ✓. row9c3 ✓. row10c2,c4 ✓. All horizontal. And any 1 in input with 9 both sides that stayed 1? Row0: c4,5,6 — need 9 both sides; rightmost 9 at c2, so no. Row3 all ones. Looks consistent.

Apply to test grid: for each row, fill 1s that have 4 on both left and right with 2.

Note test uses 4s. Demo used 9s. Assume same rule with the task color.
Demo rule confirmed: fill 1s lying between two 9s (here 4s) in the same row with 2. Submit.
